title: Native CLIC1 mediates chloride-based long-range tumor suppression

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Native CLIC1 mediates chloride-based long-range tumor suppression

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1) is required for chloride-driven, long-range suppression of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus laevis, because non-local overexpression of wildtype CLIC1 increases suppression while a dominant-negative CLIC1C24S mutant blocks suppression even under high extracellular chloride.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Chloride-dependent hyperpolarization through endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In contrast, overexpression of the mutant CLIC1 (N=336) effectively blocked ITLS suppression despite the presence of high Cl− (Fig 4C). Together, these data suggest a role for native CLIC1 in mediating hyperpolarization-induced long-range ITLS suppression.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “RESULTS › Chloride-dependent hyperpolarization through endogenous chloride intracellular channel 1 (CLIC1)”. Scope: 16-cell-stage Xenopus laevis embryos injected with KRASG12D plus wildtype or dominant-negative CLIC1 in a separate blastomere, raised in 70 mM chloride

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The paired gain- and loss-of-function design has substantial discriminating power. Public summaries allow partial checking, but raw records and controls needed to establish native CLIC1 as the unique mediator are incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Under high chloride, compare tumor incidence after remote wild-type CLIC1, dominant-negative CLIC1C24S, and matched controls while measuring Vmem. Necessity is supported if the mutant abolishes suppression and sufficiency is strengthened if wild type increases it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Direct channel-current and spatial Vmem data are limited.

Dominant-negative constructs may have off-target effects.

Individual records are not clearly public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The wild-type versus point-mutant contrast is a published measurement bearing on whether chloride-driven suppression uses CLIC1. The sample size for the blocking construct is stated. Off-target effects of the dominant-negative protein, and missing per-embryo expression and voltage, leave the requirement claim only partly checked.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Under 70 mM chloride, compare KRASG12D incidence with remote wild-type CLIC1 versus remote CLIC1C24S, and measure whether only the wild-type channel hyperpolarizes the remote tissue. Loss of suppression specifically with the dominant-negative construct would support a native CLIC1 requirement; suppression despite the mutant would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Dominant-negative overexpression can disrupt more than CLIC1 conductance.

Expression level and remote voltage for each embryo are not in a public table.

operationalizability: 0.72
